question: Which four countries make up the Quad?
solution:
The correct answer is __**USA, Japan, India, Australia**__.

**__Key Points__**

• The **Quadrilateral Security Dialogue**, commonly known as the **Quad**, is a strategic security dialogue between four nations: the **United States of America**, **India**, **Japan**, and **Australia**. These countries are committed to supporting a **free, open, and inclusive Indo-Pacific** region.

• The concept of the **Quad** was first initiated in **2007** by the then **Japanese Prime Minister Shinzo Abe**. It was supported by **US Vice President Dick Cheney**, **Australian Prime Minister John Howard**, and **Indian Prime Minister Manmohan Singh**.

• The group was revived in **2017** on the sidelines of the **ASEAN Summit** in **Manila**, **Philippines**. This revival was driven by the shared vision of the four nations to counter the growing economic and military influence of **China** in the **Indo-Pacific** and **South China Sea**.
